content.title: How to watch USA vs. Dominican Republic in 2026 World Baseball Classic semifinals
content.text: The World Baseball Classic is down to the rounds where every pitch carries consequence. Team USA is in the semifinals, and there is no soft landing waiting — only the Dominican Republic, with national pride and a spot in Tuesday’s championship game at stake.The United States got here the hard way. It opened pool play with wins over Brazil, Great Britain and Mexico, then took an 8-6 loss to Italy before regrouping to beat Canada 5-3 in the quarterfinals. The U.S. recovered, but the loss to Italy remains the blemish on its run to the semifinals. That path matters because the U.S. has looked dangerous without looking airtight, which is usually how short tournaments turn into ulcer factories.How to watch USA vs. Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic semifinals Venue: loanDepot Park — Miami Date: Sunday, March 15, 8 p.m. ET TV: FS1 Streaming: Fubo (Stream Free Now!) Watching in person? Get tickets on StubHub. Fox programs also stream with a Fox One subscription.Team USA beat Canada behind 4 2/3 scoreless innings from Logan Webb and early RBIs from Kyle Schwarber, Alex Bregman and Brice Turang. Canada made it close after Bo Naylor’s two-run homer, but David Bednar escaped a jam in the seventh and Mason Miller struck out the side in the ninth.Your browser does not support the video tag.The U.S. roster is one of the nastiest ever assembled for this event. Japan arrived as the defending champion and the tournament’s looming standard, but no two teams in the 20-country field were more packed with MLB star power than the United States and the Dominican Republic.Team USA has reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge and reigning NL Cy Young winner Paul Skenes, plus seven other players who received MVP votes last season: Cal Raleigh, Bobby Witt Jr. and Byron Buxton in the AL, and Pete Crow-Armstrong, Will Smith, Turang and Schwarber in the NL. That list doesn’t even include Tarik Skubal, the Detroit Tigers’ Cy Young winner who finished fifth in AL voting. Despite criticism from some fans, Skubal stuck with his plan to start one game for the U.S. (a 9-1 win over Great Britain) and then rejoin the Tigers.The Dominican Republic counters with nine 2025 MVP vote-getters of its own. In the AL, Julio Rodríguez, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Junior Caminero earned votes, as did Juan Soto, Geraldo Perdomo, Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado, Ketel Marte and Cristopher Sánchez in the NL.Judge is the captain for the U.S., but the game may turn on Skenes against a Dominican lineup that has mauled this tournament, outscoring opponents 51-10 so far. Managed by Albert Pujols — a prolific home run hitter in his day — the D.R. has mashed 14 HRs, tying a World Baseball Classic record.The history is worth keeping in mind. The Dominican Republic won this tournament in 2013. Team USA won it in 2017 and reached the final again in 2023 before losing to Japan. Sunday is not the final, but it has the shape of one: stars everywhere, thin margins and a championship berth on the line.Sunday’s winner will play either Venezuela or Italy, who face off in the other semifinal Monday night.Updated World Baseball Classic oddsIf you like using odds to project outcomes, Sunday’s game is expected to be a tight one. Team USA is currently a -140 favorite to win the highly anticipated game. Basically, the odds imply a about a 58 percent chance of the Americans winning. On the flip side, the Dominican Republic’s moneyline odds sit at +110.The sportsbooks also like the winner of this matchup to win it all. The Americans are currently the favorites to win the World Baseball Classic (+145 at DraftKings), with the Dominican Republic on their heels at +155. Then, there’s a big jump on the title odds board, with Venezuela at +360 and Italy at +700.Ticketing and streaming links in this article are provided by partners of The Athletic.
